doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Big bands, Lionel Hampton and boarding houses
summary: Big band travel taught him the grind of the business, with cheap YMCA rooms and boarding houses under Hampton.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Was Dud Bascomb’s band a big band?
Oh, we went out. We played...
So you did play in some big bands?
Was that a good experience, playing in big bands?
Well, because you got to travel. You got to go to towns. You got to see people.
And they got to see you, I guess.

Yeah. And you got to know the grinds of music. Because there was a certain grind you have to really go through before you get indoctrinated into the music business. Because, see, the bandleaders are always... I worked with Lionel Hampton for a while. The bandleaders always drive off to the Hilton Hotel, and stop the bus. Then you had to get out, and we had to walk down the street and find a Y, because they wasn’t payin’ no money, so we had to get the YMCA, $2 or $3 a night room. We didn’t make any money.
Were there boarding houses, too? Did you stay in people’s private houses?
How did that work? Did they differ in quality, where some were nice, some weren’t nice?
Yeah. Some were nice and some weren’t nice.
Yeah, most of them would feed you breakfast.
